desc:
perm is a permutation of the integers 0..n-1. Think of it as a set of arrows: index i points to index perm[i]. Following the arrows from any index eventually brings you back to where you started; the indices visited on the way form a cycle. Every index belongs to exactly one cycle.

Return the number of cycles. An index with perm[i] = i is a cycle of length 1.

Example: perm = [1, 0, 2, 4, 3, 5] has the cycles {0, 1}, {2}, {3, 4}, {5}, so the answer is 4.
constraints: perm is a permutation of 0..n-1 (each value exactly once)
hints: Start from an index, follow the arrows until you come back, and count that as one cycle. How do you avoid counting the same cycle again from another of its members?
Keep a visited flag for each index. Only start a new walk from an index that has not been visited yet.
Loop over all indices; whenever an index is unvisited, increase the answer and walk its whole cycle, marking every index as visited.
editorial: Because perm is a permutation, every index has exactly one arrow leaving it and exactly one arrow entering it, so the arrows split the indices into disjoint cycles (no tails). Scan the indices from left to right. If an index is not yet visited, it begins a new cycle: count it and follow the arrows, marking each index visited, until you return to the start.
Each index is marked once, so the total work is O(n) and the visited array needs O(n) bits. (The array itself can be used for marking by overwriting visited entries with -1, giving O(1) extra space.)
